standard_prerequisites.name: Homogeneous generators of a finitely generated graded algebra
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the start of the counted proof (lines 13914-13916)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the generating set to homogeneous elements, which is what makes the degree bookkeeping work.

standard_prerequisites.name: Description of elements of the dehomogenised ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Writes an element as a sum of fractions with bounded exponents, giving finitely many generators.

core_obligations: Replace the chosen generators by their homogeneous components and describe an arbitrary element of the dehomogenised ring as a sum of fractions built from the homogeneous pieces (proof lines 13914-13920).

Bound the exponents by the degree of the dehomogenising element, so that only finitely many monomials occur, which gives finite generation of the dehomogenised algebra and of the dehomogenised finite module (proof lines 13920-13943).
proof_roadmap: Write elements with bounded exponents and read off finite generation (proof lines 13916-13944).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finitely generated graded algebra S over R and a homogeneous element f of positive degree, the dehomogenised ring is of finite type over R and the dehomogenisation of any finite graded module is finite over it (statement lines 13902-13911). The proof does not present the dehomogenised pieces abstractly: it makes the generators homogeneous, writes a general element as a sum of fractions and uses the degree of f to bound the exponents, so that only finitely many monomials appear (proof lines 13913-13944). The exponent bound is what turns an a priori infinite description into a finite generating set. H2.
